thread:
maria: quick heads-up — pushed a tiny PoC for a per-model econ mini-panel to the analytics branch. want quick feedback before i wire it into the console :eyes:
ajay: nice. what's in the PoC? a lot of the earlier dashboards were too aggregated to act on.
maria: it's intentionally narrow: per-model tokens, billed tokens after cache credits, cache hit rate, effective cost/token, and a tiny suggestion engine (quantize? dense->int8?) based on cost delta. also shows route breakdown for top 5 routes calling each model.
sam: we should surface sequence-length buckets. a model can look cheap on avg but blow up at long seqs. can we show p50/p95 tokens-per-response buckets?
maria: yep — included 1–128,129–512,513+ buckets with token distribution. screenshot in the branch.
emily: how are you calculating "billed tokens after cache credits"? that's been a sticking point in past threads.
maria: good question — current PoC uses event stream join: billed = tokens - kv_cache_prefix_tokens * cache_credit_rate. It's an approximation; we flag anything with >20% estimated credit for review. SQL prototype: ```SELECT model, route, SUM(tokens) AS tokens, SUM(kv_prefix_hits) AS prefix_hits, (SUM(tokens) - SUM(kv_prefix_hits)*0.75) AS est_billed FROM token_events WHERE ts >= '2026-03-01' GROUP BY model, route;```
ajay: using 0.75 as credit rate OK for now but we need to make that param-driven (per-kv-profile). Also consider cold-start amortization for new model versions — first 24h have abnormal token mix.
ryan_infra: deployment note — if we add route breakdown for top 5 routes per model, that will add a fanout join during backfill. can we precompute heavy joins in materialized views? otherwise cost will spike.
maria: yeah planning a materialized table daily. small lambda will compute top routes and store a compressed list.
sam: UX: on the panel can we have a toggle: "show per-tenant amortized cost" vs "raw cost"? folks want both (finance vs eng).
emily: strongly +1. also add a small explain bubble: how cache savings were attributed (prefix vs kv hits vs response dedupe). prevents finger-pointing.
ajay: another thought — show an "action" column with one-click rollout guard: if effective_cost/token > threshold AND p95 latency under SLO then suggest a quantization trial. the button should create a canary rollout with preseeded eval prompts.
maria: nice. that's the plan for the next PR. UX question: should the suggested quant levels be model-suggested or workload-suggested?
emily: workload-suggested — i.e., what preserves eval score on that tenant's prompts. model-suggested is useful as a baseline but can be misleading.
ryan_infra: one more infra caveat: the sample rate for telemetry affects the accuracy of token distribution for low-volume tenants. we should surface confidence intervals (CI) when sample rate < 1%. maybe show a small warning badge.
maria: adding CI and a tooltip that explains sampling bias. also will add a "request full backfill" action that queues a higher-sweep job for the tenant (audit + cost).
sam: love the backfill action. can we gate it by billing team approval for very large backfills? to avoid unexpected infra charges.
emily: yes — add an optional approval step, default off for dev orgs.
ajay: nit: rename "effective cost" to "net unit cost" in UI copy. clearer for cross-team stakeholders.
maria: done — will update labels.
deploy-bot: Maria pushed 2154321099 -> analytics/cost-mini-panel (CI: passed) :rocket:
ryan_infra: can someone review infra changes? I'm OOO tomorrow but can triage Friday.
maria: pinging @ryan_infra for infra review, @emily for attribution copy, @ajay for rollout flow. will open a PR request thread. thanks all :+1:
